To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
most Americans would feel less safe as more people in their communities acquired firearms.

50% of respondents reported that, if more people in the community acquired guns, they would feel less rather than more safe; 50% reported that they would not feel more or less safe; 14% said they would feel more rather than less safe; 16% of women reported that they would likely feel less safe, compared to 10% of men, and 19% of Blacks and Hispanics reported that they would probably feel less safe, as compared to 11% of Whites
50% of Americans would feel less safe, 14% would feel more safe and 36% would feel equally safe if more guns were in their community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people in a community feel about the safety of their community as more people in that community own guns.
the psychological effects of firearms in a community and the influence that these firearms have on the perceptions of safety of community members.
the effects of guns in the community, not the effects of community on guns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
more guns in the community make others feel less safe.
the presence of more guns in a community makes others feel less safe.
more firearms in the community make people feel less safe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of guns in one's community is associated with a perception of less community safety.
more guns in the community make most people less safe.
more firearms in the community make others in the neighborhood less safe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to popular beliefs, guns in a community can make people feel less safe, not more safe.
the presence of more guns in the community can have a negative psychological impact on the community.
, contrary to the common perception that guns make people safer, the opposite is true.
